title: Reviving 'Down in the Tin Cup Room' and other old tunes
summary: He describes unwritten old tunes he heard at picnics and in the red-light district, which he plans to rework and write down.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Those things sell good. So I'm writing it. I'm writing it. And I don't know whether I orchestrate it or not because it's so hard to get an orchestra to. I like to have an orchestra to go over my way to see if I forgot something or if I want to put in something. Sometimes I might want to improve the phrase here or there. I might want to change the harmony just a little bit or place or another. You understand? Or I might want to put some little extra pep to it and so forth. Well, I was thinking about fixing that thing up. And there's another old tune that we used to play. It was never written. It was only a bi-tune. You know, like people make up a little tune. Oh yeah. And the band used to play. The old Spanish fort. Well, way back then when Matthew Perez was just beginning to play trumpet. I remember that as well. He was playing with a young boy that was a good violin player. I forget what his name was. Big Gasper and all of them, they were young musicians at the time. You know what I mean, playing. I was a kid. I was a little kid. I used to go out there for picnics and so forth. And they used to play a piece they called, Down in the Tin Cup Room. I know you didn't know that. Down in the Tin Cup Room. But it was only a ghost song. It was just somewhat of a Volcker song, you know?
Yeah. Some of those were, I know.

Some of the words. Yeah, and they used to sing around the red light district and so forth. But I figured on revising it and using it, not in that way, but using the idea. Down in the Tin Cup Room where I used to go, when they knocked me to the floor and took all my dough. I'm going to fix it up that way, you see? Yes. And that gives it to my heart. Remember all of them? In fact, that was never written. I'm going to write it down. Yeah, but nobody wrote that down at all, I guess. And I'm going to take them two pieces. I'm going to take them two pieces. But the only thing that I would like to get, and I was thinking very hard, there's only one person that I figured could sing better. And that's Lizzy Mahoney.
